findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple wiping cloths in the hand sink. Education was carried out. The rags were removed. Ensure that the all handwashing sinks in the facility are use for handwashing only. Keeping items in the hand sinks discourages proper handwashing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The sanitizer in the sani buckets were unreadable. PIC was made aware. The sanitizers were remade and tested at 100 ppm. Ensure that the concentration of the sanitizer is within the appropriate range at all times.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The baffles of the ice machine was observed with soil accumulations. PIC was made aware. The ice was taken out and the baffles cleaned and sanitized while inspector was present. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the ice machine baffles are monitored, cleaned and sanitized at a regular frequency.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The caulking on the triple sink was observed to be unsealed. PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the triple sink will be sealed properly.  Ensure that the caulking is re-done providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(2) A tray of cooked dumpling was observed being stored underdressed raw chicken to cool. Education was carried out and the dumpling tray was removed. Ensure that proper storage order is practiced to avoid cross contamination. 

Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Multiple soda nozzles were observed with soil accumulation. PIC was made aware. The nozzles were removed, cleaned, and sanitized. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the soda nozzles are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency. 

Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11(A) Inspector observed water chestnuts being stored in the can after opening inside the prep cooler. Education was carried out. The chestnuts were placed in the appropriate storage container. Ensure that food items are stored appropriately to avoid contamination. 

Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed staff members bare hands in single service containers while pouring ready to eat food items in the containers. PIC was made aware that such bare handling could lead to contamination. Education was carried out and the behavior was corrected. Ensure that staff are knowledgeable when handling ready to eat food items. Hence, hands must be washed and gloves donned in such process.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed dirty mop water being stored in the mop bucket. Discussed with PIC and the mop bucket was drained into the utility sink. Ensure that such wastewater is properly drained to avoid the harboring of pests and bacteria growth.
findings.citation_text: 5-403.12 Other Liquid Wastes and Rainwater. Condensate drainage and other nonSEWAGE liquids and rainwater shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to LAW.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The baffle of the ice machine was observed to have an accumulation of pink and black molds on its surface. Discussed with PIC and an employee was instructed to note the location when cleaning the ice machine. Ensure that this item is observed and cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain it clean and sanitized.[P]
findings.citation_text: 4-602.11(A) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (A) Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned: (1) Except as specified in (B) of this section, before each use with a different type of raw animal FOOD such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, or POULTRY; (2) Each time there is a change from working with raw FOODS to working with READY-TO-EAT FOODS; (3) Between uses with raw fruits and vegetables and with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD; (4) Before using or storing a FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE; and (5) At any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: A packet of shrimp was observed in a bowl of water at the top of the triple sink to be thawed. PIC was made aware of appropriate thawing methods. The bowl with the shrimp was placed under running water for appropriate thawing. Ensure that staffs are aware of the adequate thawing methods to avoid the contamination of food items. [Pf]
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: A live roach was observed under the hand sink at the end of the cook line. PIC was made aware f the presence of pest and PIC ensured that a pest control company was going to be called to handle the presence of pest. Ensure that facility is routinely checked for pest presence and activities. [C]
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following areas were observed to indicate the accumulation of soils and food debris.
1. Accumulated grease under the grill and oven on the cook-line.
2. Food debris under the prep cooler across from the cook-line
3. The walk-in freezer was observed to have spilled food debris on the floor. 
Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured that adequate cleaning will be done. Ensure that these areas are cleaned to remove their current buildup of residues and that surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable. [C]
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
Observed there is not signed employee health reporting forms for all employees. The PIC had blank copies of the reporting forms and has some forms signed by current employees. Ensure that all employees sign employee health reporting forms. 

2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed the following food in the walk-in cooler was not protected from cross contamination during storage: (1) Raw chicken stored above sauce with a saran-warp lid that was only half covering the top and a container missing a lid; and (2) Date marking sticky notes on top of food. The above mentioned sauces with improper lids were moved from below the chicken. The sticky notes were removed from the food and stuck on the side of the containers holding the food. Ensure that food is protected from cross contamination during storage.

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
Observed the standing freezer and the standing clear door cooler do not have internal thermometers. Ensure that all refrigerated food storage units have temperature meaning devices. There will be a follow-up on 07/22/2024 to ensure the sanding freezer and standing clear door coolers have thermometers. 

4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

findings.comment:
Observed batter stored in tubs sitting on the floor. Ensure that food is stored at least 6-inches off the flood to prevent contamination. The batter was moved off the floor during the inspection.

(C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.18: The cooler that is used to hold the par-cooked chicken and the beef is observed to be out of temperature. According to the PIC, this cooler went out of temp sometime this morning with an unknown start time. During the inspection, the cooler temperature was internally checked by probing food items, which registered at 53 degrees F with an ambient air temperature of 58 degrees F. With an unknown start time of temperature abuse, the entire cooler is being voluntarily discarded of all remaining food items. PIC is ordering a new cooler to utilize in its place. A spot check will be conducted on Monday, 7/10/23, to observe the cooler replaced, repaired, or not in use. 
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C): The employees of the facility have not completed a food handler certification course. PIC asked for a link to an ANSI accredited certification course that is offered in Chinese. The inspector will forward the PIC a link to an ANSI accredited food handler course. Each employee needs to have a food handlers and have their food handler certification in a verifiable manner.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C): Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.comment: 3-304.12: A knife was observed stored between the prep tables along the cook line. This knife was removed from service and placed into the wash, rinse, sanitize cycle. Ensure that in use utensils are stored in a manner that prevents contamination of the food contact surface. 3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The hand sink is observed to have a very loose faucet. Ensure this item is reattached to create a secure seal for the faucet attached to the sink basin.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: Observed multiple employees go from one task to another without washing their hands after contamination occurs. Inspector had a discussion with the PIC about hand washing and to ensure retraining and education are given to their staff regarding hand washing. Ensure hand washing is completed to ensure contamination does not occur of the food being handled.
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: The hand sink was observed to have multiple rags in the basin which inhibited employees form accessing the hand sink. These rags were removed immediately and education was provided to the PIC as to why having the hand sink clear is crucial to contamination prevention. Ensure this hand sink remains clear and is only used for hand washing.
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: The sanitizer bucket was observed to have been used with soap as there were many bubbles present. It was confirmed by the employees that soap was indeed mistakingly used instead of bleach. This bucket was immediately dumped and filled with fresh warm water and bleach at a concentration of 100ppm. Ensure the sanitizer bucket is at least 100ppm bleach to be used for sanitizing the kitchen surfaces.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: Many areas in the kitchen, including, but not limited to the shelves and under hard to reach areas, are observed to be in need of a detailed cleaning. Ensure detailed cleaning is performed at a frequency necessary to prevent the accumulation of soil residues.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: The shelving units int he back of the facility are observed to have missing or shipped paint which has exposed bare wood. THis bare wood needs to be resealed by using a sealant such  as paint to make the surface smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable.
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: In the walk-in cooler, raw chicken was observed to be stored in a container above cooked fried rice. The chicken was moved during the inspection to prevent the potential contamination of the rice. Ensure proper storage practices are followed to ensure the safety and the integrity of the food remains.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: The bleach sanitizer bucket registered at a level below 50ppm when tested. Bleach was added to the solution during the inspection and registered at 100-200ppm. Ensure that the test strips are regularly utilized to ensure the sanitizer concentration is sufficient enough to accomplish the sanitization process.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10).

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: There were observed multiple wiping cloths on the counter being used to wipe off surfaces and then stored on the counter surface. These rags were placed into the corrected sanitizer solution during the inspection. Ensure the rags are placed into the sanitizer solution between uses to prevent cross contamination from the rag’s surface to the object being cleaned and sanitized.
3-304.14: (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: Multiple surfaces in the facility are in need of a general cleaning. These surfaces include the floor, wall, and shelving. Ensure these items are cleaned at a frequency to prevent soil and residue accumulation and the deter the presence of pests.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: When the inspector went to wash their hands, it was noted that there were no paper towels available. During the hand washing, a roll of paper towels was brought to the inspector. Ensure that the hand sink is always supplied with soap, paper towels, and a trash can nearby.
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: It was observed during the start of the inspection that there was no sanitizer bucket made and ready to use. Inspector provided education to the facility that during any hours of operation or during any prep work there must be a sanitizer bucket available with 100-200ppm of bleach. The sanitizer bucket was created during the time of the inspection and recorded using test strips to be between 100-200ppm bleach solution.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10).

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: It was observed that the tongs in the prep table were stored with the handles touching the foods. This action was corrected by the inspector on sight and reeducating the staff was performed by the PIC on how to properly store the in use utensils to prevent contamination.
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container
